steps.body: Cubes make good units because they are all the same size and stack end to end without gaps.
steps.narration: Cubes make good units because they are all the same size and stack end to end without gaps.

widget.prompt: Measure the scarf with one-unit cubes — eight, touching end to end.
widget.successFeedback: Eight identical cubes cover the scarf exactly, so the scarf is eight cubes long.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Why do cubes work well as measuring units?

options.label: They are all the same size

predict.reveal: Identical size is the whole requirement; color and material make no difference to a count.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1m cubes.

misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

explanationVariants: Units must be identical to each other.

widget.prompt: Exactly 9 same-size cubes cover a ribbon with no gaps and no overlaps. How long is the ribbon in cubes? Choose the key measurement idea.

options.feedback: That counts one unit more than were actually placed along the object.
That misses one of the units that helped cover the object.
That doubles the count, as if each unit were counted twice over.
Correct — the length is the number of same-size units that cover it end to end, which is 9.

widget.prompt: Measure a new cube train: six identical one-unit cubes cover it end to end.
widget.successFeedback: Six identical cubes cover the train exactly, so its length is six cubes.
widget.alignFeedback: Begin at the train's first edge so the cubes cover every part of its length.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Cubes must touch without spaces or overlaps for the count to be true.
widget.unitFeedback: Every cube must be the same size before its count can measure a length.

widget.prompt: A child lays 4 cubes along a stick but leaves small spaces between them. What is true of the count? Use a fresh measurement clue.

options.label: The count is fine either way
options.feedback: Units must cover the object completely; uncovered stretches are simply never counted.

options.label: The count is wrong — gaps hide length
options.feedback: Correct — every gap leaves length uncounted, so the measurement comes out too small.

options.label: Gaps make the count too large
options.feedback: Gaps mean fewer units are used, so the count comes out too small rather than too large.

options.label: Only overlaps matter, not gaps
options.feedback: Both spoil a measurement: overlaps count length twice and gaps miss length entirely.
